articles.title: Vizio’s discounted Mini LED TV lets you skip the sign-ups and smarts
articles.content: Walmart’s inexpensive Vizio produces a nice, bright image, though its black levels aren’t that deep. | Photo: John Higgins / The Verge Modern smart TVs let you skip the streaming device, which is convenient, but they also come with their own issues, including privacy concerns and frequent updates. The Vizio Mini LED Quantum TV lets you cut out the rigamarole and just get straight to the HDMI ports. And right now, it’s discounted at Walmart, with the 65-inch model going for $358 ($40 off) and the 85-inch model going for $698 ($100 off). Vizio Mini LED Quantum TV Where to Buy: $278 $248 at Walmart (55-inch) $398 $358 at Walmart (65-inch) $768 $698 at Walmart (85-inch) Although Vizio’s Mini LED TV comes loaded with Vizio OS, you can bypass the TV’s host of agreements during setup. By pushing past the manufacturer’s warnings about “missing out” on smart TV features, you can disable the built-in operating system, letting you use your own streaming device like a Roku or Apple TV 4K without worrying about what data Vizio and Walmart might be collecting. As for specs, the TV features quantum dots for full, vivid color and high brightness (our testing showed it can reach 936 nits when calibrated thanks to its mini-LED panel). There are some compromises, though, which is expected given the low price point. The IPS panel doesn’t have the best black levels, as you might see on more expensive sets, and there’s a touch of motion blur during faster scenes, which may also hurt its appeal for gamers. It also has three HDMI ports, but they’re only 2.0, although the screen only supports up to 4K at 60Hz, so it’s not detrimental to the experience. Read our full Vizio Mini LED Quantum TV review .
articles.author: Brad Bourque

articles.title: NFL Week 8 preview: 5 games you can’t miss this weekend
articles.content: Elite offenses meet elite defenses, malfunctioning defenses meet elite offenses, and hapless offenses meet elite defenses in Week 8 of the NFL season, with a potential NFC Championship dress-rehearsal thrown in for good measure. Chicago's Monday night showdown with Seattle serves as a fitting crescendo to one of the best slates of the campaign so far. Here's our pick of the top five NFL Week 8 games — and where to watch NFL online and on TV. 🏈 Watch NFL from anywhere with IPVanish (83% off) Vikings at Lions Sunday, 1 p.m. ET, FOX/Fox One FREE on 5 (U.K.) FREE on 7Plus (Australia) FREE on TVNZ+ (New Zealand) The Vikings are the only undefeated team in the NFL, but are they actually any good? Brian Flores' defense certainly is, but with a mere 10 offensive touchdowns, kicker Will Reichard having outscored every other Viking combined , a dip in form is surely coming. Cue Jared Goff and the freewheeling Lions offense. Unfortunately for Detroit, their defense is about as bad as Minnesota's offense and they've lost two straight to their NFC North rivals. This will be fascinating. Ravens at Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. ET, CBS/Paramount+ A variation on the theme, the Ravens' clash with the Bills has the potential to be a shootout, seeing as both defenses are awful and both offenses are outstanding — if Lamar Jackson plays, that is. The Baltimore star's apparently imminent return from an ankle injury has failed to materialize for a month now, perhaps with this Week 8 fixture in mind. In the meantime, the Ravens have dropped to the bottom of the AFC North after blowing double-digit leads in each of their past two games. Josh Allen and the Bills, meanwhile, are fresh from a bye. Chargers at Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET, FOX/Fox One FREE on 7Plus (Australia) FREE on TVNZ+ (New Zealand) The L.A. derby is shaping up as an expensive box office flop instead of the blockbuster it was supposed to be, but it should be fun regardless. The Chargers are now the only winless team in the NFL, but they've had a full fortnight to straighten things out on the training pitch and prepare for the misfiring preseason favorites. Unfortunately for Jim Harbaugh, the Rams were unrecognizable last weekend, as they tore up the usual game plan and put it all on running backs Blake Corum and Kyren Williams — and it worked so effectively Sean McVay would be bonkers to change tack. Chiefs at Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET, CBS/Paramount+ FREE on 5 (U.K.) FREE on Virgin Media Play (Ireland) The Chiefs' opening weekend encounter with the Broncos was a total mismatch, but the AFC West rivals are trending in different directions now. articles.title: UK Social Media Ban May Lock Out More Than 100,000 Teens Without ID
articles.content: Under the UK's planned social media ban, more than 100,000 British teenagers aged 16 and 17 could initially be locked out of social media because they lack a passport or driving license that may be needed as a fallback for age verification. The Guardian reports: Ofcom, the UK's online watchdog, said about 150,000 16- to 17-year-olds do not own a passport or driving licence, which are likely to be needed to access age-restricted platforms. The Australia-style ban on under-16s accessing social media services, including Instagram, TikTok and YouTube, is due to come into force next spring. The head of Ofcom, Melanie Dawes, said "motivated children" would seek to bypass the restrictions, as has happened in Australia. On Thursday, Ofcom published an assessment of age verification measures that could underpin the ban, outlining four "highly effective" methods: checking a person's official ID against a live selfie, a bank verifying an account holder's age, an official digital ID service like the Young Scot card, or estimating someone's age via a selfie. However, the watchdog said a form of official ID would probably be needed as a "backstop" for other methods, such as facial age estimation, which could be inaccurate by several years. Ofcom said a cohort of 16- to 17-year-olds could miss out as a result. "This means that people without a form of photo ID will likely need to take steps to obtain one to access age-restricted services," the regulator said. The report notes that more than nine out of 10 Britons over 16 have passports or driving licenses. "We should expect that motivated children will seek to bypass the restrictions -- just like alcohol laws can't completely eradicate underage drinking -- but there'll be ways for platforms to mitigate this risk," said Dawes. "This will be a huge cultural shift for our society, so it'll take time to adjust, and everyone will have a part to play." Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Thousands of “ghost students” use AI to steal millions in student loans, DOJ says
articles.content: The US has charged five individuals as part of the first broad federal crackdown on “ghost students”—fraudsters who steal the identities of hundreds of Americans to pose as fake college students and steal student loans. In a press release Thursday, the Department of Justice said it had uncovered a large-scale scheme relying partly on AI. The DOJ seized more than $750,000 in cryptocurrency from “a network associated with Kenyan nationals" after data analysis helped flag likely fraudsters. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the DOJ’s National Fraud Enforcement Division credited new fraud-detection measures implemented by the Trump administration for the arrests. He said that “this is the first international seizure of its kind in Kenya,” while warning fraudsters that the crackdown has only just begun. “If you steal American identities, if you steal taxpayer dollars, if you exploit programs meant to help students build a future—we will find you,” McDonald said. “Whether you are in Nebraska, New Jersey, Virginia, or Nairobi, we will pursue you.” Read full article Comments

articles.title: The MacRumors Show: OLED MacBook Pro, iPad Mini 8, and More
articles.content: On this week's episode of The MacRumors Show , we discuss Apple's newly announced OLED MacBook Pro , iPad mini with A20 Pro, and M6 versions of the iMac and entry-level 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌. Subscribe to The MacRumors Show YouTube channel for more videos The MacBook Pro gains a tandem ‌OLED‌ display with touch support for the first time. Available in 14- and 16-inch sizes, the "PROLED XDR display" offers up to 2,000 nits of peak HDR and SDR brightness, a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio, and Adobe RGB support alongside P3. Touch input enables gestures such as scrolling, pinching to zoom, and dragging content, with a reinforced hinge and camera stabilization designed to accommodate interaction with the screen. A Dynamic Island replaces the notch, providing access to Live Activities, Siri AI, and more. The enclosure is thinner and lighter , with the 14-inch model weighing 3 pounds and the 16-inch model weighing 4 pounds. The larger model's display grows to 16.3 inches, and the iconic illuminated Apple logo returns. The new models retain the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips introduced earlier this year, but add a redesigned thermal architecture and upgraded speakers with 50% deeper bass and dedicated tuning for closed-lid playback. Maximum storage doubles to 16TB . Pricing starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch model, a $400 premium over comparable mini-LED configurations. The new ‌iPad mini‌ moves from an 8.3-inch LCD to an 8.5-inch ‌OLED‌ display, with thinner borders, up to 1,200 nits of peak HDR brightness, and a nano-texture option on the 256GB and 512GB configurations. It is thinner and lighter at 5.4mm thick, and becomes the first iPad with an official IP67 water and dust resistance rating. The display remains limited to 60Hz, with no ProMotion support . The A20 Pro chip brings GPU Neural Accelerators and increased memory bandwidth to the device, with Apple claiming up to 60% faster CPU performance, 2.7 times faster graphics, and 4.5 times faster AI performance than the previous generation. The 512GB configuration has an additional CPU core and a second 16-core Neural Engine compared with the 128GB and 256GB models. An all-new Acoustic Display speaker system eliminates external speaker holes, while the front camera moves to the landscape edge and the rear camera gains an Adaptive True Tone flash . Other additions include fast charging , Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread, Apple's C2 modem on cellular models, and extended external display support with iPadOS 27.2. The ‌iPad mini‌ starts at $699 in Midnight or Starlight , with a new $79 TechWoven Smart Folio available separately. The M6 iMac replaces the M4 model, adding two CPU and GPU cores to both the two-port and four-port configurations. It also gains GPU Neural Accelerators, dual 16-core Neural Engines, up to twice as fast SSD storage, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread, and 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet . Pricing starts at $1,499, with the four-port model starting at $1,699. The entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro moves from M5 to M6, with a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, dual 16-core Neural Engines, and upgraded wireless connectivity. Memory bandwidth increases to 170GB/s on 24GB and 32GB configurations, while the 16GB model remains at 153GB/s. Its $1,999 starting price and battery life of up to 24 hours carry over from the outgoing model. All four products are available to pre-order now and launch on November 6. articles.title: GM cracks the petty cash box for multistate driver tracking settlement
articles.content: General Motors is taking what looks like a light slap on the wrist from a coalition of 35 states and the District of Columbia after agreeing to settle allegations that it collected drivers' data without proper consent and sold it to data brokers that supplied insurance companies. The Washington state AG's office said on Thursday that GM had reached a $220 million settlement with 36 attorneys general over the automaker's collection and sharing of driving data, including precise location information, speed, seatbelt use, and other metrics. According to investigators, GM sold that data to brokers, which in turn supplied it to insurance companies that could use it to set customers' premiums, without drivers' informed consent. For reference, the $220 million settlement, which will be distributed among the participating jurisdictions, equates to less than 7 percent of GM's $3.3 billion in net income attributable to stockholders for its third quarter , which ended on September 30, 2026. Don't spend it all in one place, y'all. The settlement comes more than two years after a 2024 New York Times investigation found that GM had been selling the data collected from vehicle owners through its Smart Driver program. That program, part of GM subsidiary OnStar’s offering, collected the aforementioned data and handed it back to vehicle owners in reports designed to inform better driving habits. Unbeknownst to Smart Driver subscribers, their data was also being forked over to data brokers despite GM telling customers it wouldn't share that information with insurers without their express consent. The insurers ultimately obtained the data by purchasing it from brokers with which GM had struck deals. To make matters worse, the Washington AG's office said GM incentivized dealerships to enroll customers in Smart Driver, with employees in some cases accepting terms and conditions on customers' behalf without their knowledge or consent. GM also failed to notify many drivers that their information was being collected and shared. Its OnStar app incorrectly told more than 370,000 drivers they were not enrolled in Smart Driver, even as GM continued collecting and selling their data, according to investigators. “The data GM sold was personal, identifiable, and specific,” the AG’s office said. GM canned the Smart Driver program in April 2024, just over a month after the New York Times exposed its data-sharing practices, citing customer feedback. In addition to the monetary pittance it’s handing over to the states, GM also agreed with the 36 AGs to limit the driving data it collects, better protect customer PII, and establish a "comprehensive data privacy program.” The Washington AG’s office described its settlement as “significantly stronger than any other resolution reached with GM for this conduct.” Speaking of those other terms, GM finalized its settlement of the same allegations with the Federal Trade Commission in January 2026. The FTC order required GM to obtain drivers' express consent before collecting, using, or sharing covered driving data, subject to certain exceptions. It also required the company to offer a simple way for drivers to request a copy of their data, request its deletion, and disable precise geolocation data collection where their vehicles support it. The state of California separately reached a $12.75 million settlement with GM in the matter in May; a separate case in Texas is ongoing. “This agreement … reinforces steps we’ve taken to strengthen our privacy practices,” a GM spokesperson told The Register , though the company noted that it still stands by driver data collection as a best practice. “Safer, more helpful and personalized experiences are enabled by connected vehicle data, and GM is committed to being clear about what information is used, how it’s protected, and the choices customers have about what they share,” the spokesperson added. ®

articles.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Physical AI And Predictions Lead The Lineup
articles.content: Want to keep track of the largest startup funding deals in 2026 with our curated list of $100 million-plus venture deals to U.S.-based companies? Check out The Crunchbase Megadeals Board . This is a weekly feature that runs down the week’s Top 10 announced funding rounds in the U.S. Check out last week’s biggest funding deal roundup here . This week featured a robust lineup of large rounds, led by manufacturing startup Re:Build , which closed on $2.1 billion, and predictions marketplace Kalshi , which picked up another $1 billion. Other sectors in which startups drew significant rounds included construction automation, biotech, batteries and enterprise AI. 1. Re:Build , $2.1B, manufacturing: Re:Build, a manufacturing startup that partners with industrial companies and innovators from the product design phase to large-scale production, secured $2.1 billion in new funding. General Catalyst and JPMorganChase led the financing for the 6-year-old, Framingham, Massachusetts-based company. 2. Kalshi , $1B, predictions marketplace: Predictions marketplace Kalshi announced a $1 billion Series G financing led by Wellington Management and Sequoia Capital . The round set a $40 billion post-money valuation for New York-based Kalshi, which says its business’ annualized trading volume now exceeds $1 trillion. 3. Bedrock Robotics , $600M, construction tech: San Francisco-based Bedrock Robotics, a developer of autonomous systems for heavy equipment used in construction, raised $600 million in Series C funding led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital . The round brings Bedrock’s total funding to nearly $1 billion and sets a post-money valuation of $4.1 billion. 4. Dren Bio , $350M, biotech: Dren Bio, a developer of antibody therapeutics for cancer and autoimmune diseases, closed on $350 million in a new round led by Juvia Group and Lightspeed Venture Partners . The funding will support advanced trials for the San Carlos, California-based company’s blood cancer therapies. 5. Group 14 Technologies , $169M, battery tech: Woodinville, Washington-based Group 14 Technologies, a manufacturer and supplier of advanced silicon battery materials, picked up $169 million in Series D extension funding. The company also announced plans to expand into Europe with a production facility in Sagunto, Spain. 6. (tied) Firehawk Aerospace , $150M, defense tech: Firehawk Aerospace, a developer of propulsion technology, said it secured over $150 million in Series D funding at a valuation of more than $1.4 billion. Advent and Rochefort led the financing for the 7-year-old, Dallas-based company. 6. (tied) Serval , $150M, enterprise AI: Serval, a startup focused on coding agents for enterprise automation, raised $150 million in Series C funding at a $3 billion valuation. Sequoia Capital led the round for the 2-year-old, San Francisco-based company. 8. (tied) General Compute , $100M, AI infrastructure: AI cloud provider General Compute picked up $100 million in Series A funding led by Blackbird and Abstract . The company is building out its infrastructure using inference chips from Nvidia rivals Cerebras Systems , SambaNova and Positron AI . 8. (tied) Foundry Robotics , $100M, autonomous factories: Emeryville, California-based Foundry Robotics, a startup focused on building and operating autonomous factories, closed on $100 million in a Series A funding round led by Marlinspike . 8(tied) Hex Technologies , $100M, data analytics: Hex Technologies, a startup focused on building an AI-native platform for data analytics, secured $100 million in new financing. Peak XV and 137 Ventures led the round, which set a $1.2 billion valuation for the San Francisco-based company. Methodology We tracked the largest announced rounds in the Crunchbase database that were raised by U.S.-based companies for the period of Oct. 24-30, 2026. Although most announced rounds are in the database, there may be a small time lag, as some rounds are reported late in the week. Illustration: Dom Guzman

articles.title: OpenAI CEO says it's 'quite terrible' for your PC to have RAM — Sam Altman says data centers offer better utilization
articles.content: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has data centers full of memory, but seemingly it's the 32GB of RAM in your desktop that's the problem. In an interview over beers with the YouTube channel Cheeky Pint, Altman said that local inference, and, by extension, people having DRAM in computers at home, is "quite terrible." Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft) The data center cooling state of play The custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the price GTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this year Demand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible When discussing local inference on home computers with open-source models, Altman discussed the assumption that people will be able to run local AI on their own computers, the ones they may already own or want to build. Then he explained why that's a bad idea (at the 29-minute mark): "From a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5% of the time," Altman said. "You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply-constrained environment. And somehow many people's intuition is the opposite of that." While OpenAI does have some open-source models, its primary business is in closed-source models that run in data centers, so he's really defending the company's business model. OpenAI isn't exactly threatened by some laptops and gaming rigs just yet, but local AI could mean people one day paying less for subscriptions to models like GPT-6 Luna if they have the power to run them at home. Altman's talk suggests that the company would prefer that more RAM go to OpenAI's data centers rather than home computers, which also sparks enthusiast fears of not being able to own your own hardware or software, but rather rent an agent and a computer in the cloud. Some of what Altman is saying is based on an idea that data center buildouts won't slow down. It also assumes that RAM being used in AI data centers 24/7 is more worthwhile than RAM that is used for spreadsheets, web browsing, gaming, and maybe even local AI occasionally. The rest of the wide-ranging interview includes talk of this week's PHP vulnerabilities, sandboxing models in training, and OpenAI's research in mathematics.

articles.title: Anthropic: That Claude Code extension compromise… couldn't be us
articles.content: Anthropic has denied allegations that a malicious version of the official Claude Code extension published to Cursor’s marketplace was linked to any kind of compromise of its own systems. The company was forced to issue a statement after prominent figures in the cybersecurity industry alleged that the extension, which infected up to 5,000 developers, was uploaded to Cursor’s marketplace following a breach at Claudemaker Towers. Felix Rieseberg, a member of Anthropic’s technical staff, Xeeted today: "We're working with Cursor on this incident, but it wasn’t a compromise of Anthropic's systems or employee laptops. "A malicious actor used access to Cursor's marketplace to publish a tampered copy of the Claude Code extension, which we didn't build or publish. The versions on our official channels are not affected, and this only impacts Cursor users." First spotted by EDR vendor Phorion , an unknown party pushed an update to Cursor's official Claude Code extension for Visual Studio Code that contained a persistent SSH backdoor written for Windows, macOS, and Linux. According to Cursor, the extension – version 2.1.313 – was available to download for around 11 hours between 0227 and 1335 PT (0927 and 2035 UTC) on Thursday. The vendors' analyses of the implant revealed that it collected information about the host machine and user, including usernames, configured Git emails, and public IP addresses, as well as attempting to open a reverse SSH tunnel. Crucially, Cursor echoed Phorion's assessment that the package contained a critical flaw. The script responsible for opening the SSH tunnel required admin rights on macOS and Windows to do so, and in the vast majority of cases it did not have these, resulting in failure. Regardless, the extension still forwards the collected host and user data to the attacker, as well as dropping the attacker's SSH key and installing the persistence mechanism, so developers must go threat hunting in case their instance allows for the SSH tunnel to be created successfully. Simply installing the latest version of the extension is not enough to clear the persistence mechanism, either. The full details of how to remediate the issue, and links to download scripts to wipe the infection, are laid out in Cursor's account of the situation . Aside from Rieseberg's statement today, neither Cursor nor Anthropic have commented on how the malicious package made its way to the official marketplace. Anthropic's position is that a malicious actor uploaded the tampered copy to Cursor , but the latter has not outlined how it reached the marketpplace. "[We] removed the malicious version from the marketplace immediately upon detection and blocked further distribution," Cursor said in the advisory. "We followed with a full shutdown of the VSCode Marketplace out of an abundance of caution." It also ran checks to confirm no other extensions were compromised in the same way, rotated its own keys before restoring the marketplace, and worked with a cloud hosting provider to block the connection to the attacker's server, it said. ®

articles.title: Smplify wants a human checkpoint between AI agents and your device fleet
articles.content: One of the great things about Apple device management solutions is that the market for them is growing . Another is that because no two enterprises are alike, there is scope to bring different offerings to the market. I spoke with Ben Greiner, co-founder and COO of Smplify , a new-to-market device management vendor, to find out what his company provides to IT. Smplify, which just announced $1m in pre-seed funding , offers what could be described as a headless management tool: everything it does is available through the API and CLI. In use, that means you can build it and wield it from within the tools you already use, Greiner explained. He’s building the company with Preetham Gurram, known in device management circles for his work at MobileIron, SOTI, Automox, Addigy, Scalefusion, and Apple, where he contributed to Apple’s core MDM platforms and zero-touch enrollment at scale. So, who needs this? “Device management still assumes a person is watching,” said Greiner. “Admins already automate with scripts and pipelines, and now AI agents are showing up that can act on a fleet at machine speed.” The challenge for IT is that AI is beginning to take actions, rather than suggest them. That means IT must put systems in place to manage and audit the actions AI takes. “Enterprises that win won’t be the ones with the smartest agents; they’ll be the ones that can say exactly what each agent is allowed to do and prove what it did,” he said. That’s a fair assessment of how things stand. OneTrust’s 2026 AI-ready governance report found that 87% of organizations are encouraging the use of AI agents, but only 47% have clear governance and controls in place. That’s a problem waiting for a disaster. A recent report from Gartner predicts that 40% of enterprises will demote or decommission autonomous AI agents in the coming months (“by 2027”) because of governance gaps detected only after incidents take place. Patching those gaps is expected to become a big business. Who watches the watchmen? Once agents can submit changes at lightning speed, who can approve them? How widely deployed can those changes be? The risk is “an agent with the right key can wipe thousands of laptops before anyone notices,” Greiner told me. This is a matter of AI governance and is something I know is in the thoughts of leaders at other device management companies, including Jamf and Fleet . “AI is happening whether organizations know it or not. That’s the problem. You can try to block it, but that’s very hard to do well. It’s far better to build visibility and governance around it,” Jamf CEO Beth Tschida told me earlier this year . Jamf launched its own AI Governance suite in July, focused on AI tool discovery, policy enforcement, and reporting. The Smplify approach puts some of these decisions into the management workflow itself. “Preetham calls it the last-mile control plane: the final checkpoint between what an agent decides and what actually happens on a device,” Greiner said. What are the risks of unmanaged AI? While most of the conversation is focused on the risk of data leakage or malware, the other risk is lack of accountability. What if an agent gets bad instructions or hallucinates an inappropriate solution to a problem, and then pushes a destructive change across the fleet? By then it’s too late to figure out why it happened and becomes a potentially costly damage limitation exercise. Fleet CEO Mike McNeil pointed out that part of the risk lies in the difficulty and cost of recovery after an incident . “I’d frame risk by two things: how much privilege the code runs with and how hard recovery is,” he said, noting the risk of scripts running at root, which can take full control of the machine to the extent that reversion can’t undo what’s done. Greiner thinks the way to minimize the impact of such damage is to create strong rules and boundaries, and to ensure any risky actions are held back pending human approval. articles.title: 3 new to Paramount+ movies you need to stream this weekend — including one of the best psychological thrillers in decades (Oct. 30-Nov. 1)
articles.content: It's Halloween weekend, and Paramount+ is serving up plenty of treats with a bunch of new movies to add to your watchlist. Endlessly scrolling for what to watch next can easily eat up your evening, so we cut through the clutter to shine a spotlight on the three must-watch titles that just landed on one of the best streaming services . From the edge-of-your-seat survival documentary "Hanging by a Wire" to David Fincher’s razor-sharp psychological thriller "Gone Girl" and the cringe-comedy antics of Steve Carell and Paul Rudd in "Dinner for Schmucks," there is something on this list to match whatever the vibe you're going for with your next movie night. So grab your popcorn, and read on for the three movies you need to stream on Paramount+ this weekend. 'Hanging By a Wire' (2026) "Hanging by a Wire," a nail-biting new documentary on Paramount+ follows a single terrifying day in August 2023 in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan when a cable car malfunction left eight people stranded more than 900 feet off the ground. After one of the chair-lift cables snapped, the terrified passengers, including six children, were literally hanging by a wire as officials on the ground rushed to stage a rescue. Among them were the fathers of some of the boys, a journalist covering the story, the district police chief coordinating rescue efforts, a helicopter pilot, a cable car operator, and two zipliners who together recount an unforgettable day. “Hanging by a Wire” earned a strong 87% score on Rotten Tomatoes , and has been selected as Pakistan’s first documentary submission for the international feature Oscar race. Watch "Hanging By a Wire" on Paramount+ now 'Gone Girl' (2014) For one of the best psychological thrillers of the past 15 years, look no further than "Gone Girl," master filmmaker David Fincher's hit adaptation of Gillian Flynn's 2012 bestselling novel. It’s the kind of movie that sinks its hooks into you from the get-go, with a real sense of momentum and twists that will leave your jaw on the floor. On the day of their fifth wedding anniversary, Nick Dunne (Ben Affleck) comes home to find his wife, Amy (Rosamund Pike), has disappeared. As the search gets underway, it quickly devolves into a viral media circus, as Amy is a minor celebrity for being the inspiration for her parents' acclaimed children's book series. Public sympathy drains to suspicion, however, when all the dots don't quite line up in Nick's story .... Watch "Gone Girl" on Paramount+ starting November 1 'Dinner for Schmucks' (2010) A lot of forgettable comedies came out in the 2010s, and "Dinner for Schmucks" has all the hallmarks of them: arguably too much gross-out humor, a bloated cast of comedy talent, Steve Carell at the height of his "Office" fame. Still, I have a soft spot for this terribly endearing screwball comedy, in part because, to this day, my friends and I quote Carell's inspirational speech near the end. It's good dumb fun that'll warm your heart. A group of L.A. financiers meets regularly for dinner that doubles as a competition: who can bring the best idiot along as a guest for everyone to make fun of. The 1998 French film on which it's based, "Le Dîner des Cons," is meaner and funnier, but Paul Rudd is charming as a corporate ladder climber just slimy enough to get in on this circus when he finds the holy grail of schmucks: a taxidermist with a heart of gold (Carell). Jemaine Clement also makes an unhinged cameo as the hairiest artist known to man. articles.title: Analysts find looming launch crisis is "more severe" than anticipated
articles.content: A new report from the analytics firm Quilty Space confirms that, outside of China, the world faces a significant shortage of rockets over the next five years. The firm estimates that between now and 2030, there will be a shortfall of about 150 launches compared to demand from satellite operators and civil space agencies. If demand from the US military is added in—and SpaceX does not extend the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy program to accommodate increased national security needs—the shortage could be doubled. "What we wanted to get at is to understand how severe this launch crisis is and when will it be resolved," said Caleb Henry, director of research at Quilty Space. "What we learned is that the launch crisis is more severe than we thought and that it will not go away this decade for sure, and it might not abate until sometime late in the 2030s." articles.title: Proof of Usefulness Hackathon Final Winners Announced 🎉
articles.content: Once you discover truly useful software, it’s hard to ignore. It finds its way into your life and workflow, helping you answer a nagging question, finish tasks more efficiently, make faster decisions, or solve a problem that existing tools made more complicated than it needed to be. Before long, you might even start to wonder how you ever got by without it. When we launched the Proof of Usefulness Hackathon in January, we wanted to give the people building these kinds of solutions a platform, along with a share of $150,000 in cash prizes and software credits to help them keep building. Alongside Bright Data , Neo4j , Algolia , and Storyblok , we invited builders to show us what their projects could do and provide the evidence to back it up. And boy, did they show up. Over the course of the hackathon, we received hundreds of submissions and published just shy of 300 stories on the #proof-of-usefulness-hackathon page. Behind those numbers are builders who took the time to share their work, explain the problems they were tackling, and put their progress out there for others to examine. To everyone who submitted a project, published a report, or spent time discovering what others had built: thank you for making this hackathon's inaugural edition a success. In May, we announced our first set of winners , recognizing projects across all five award categories. Today, we’re closing out the hackathon with the final round of winners . This round covers the remaining $118,000 in prizes , comprising $12,000 in cash and $106,000 in software credits , distributed across the following categories: AWARD CATEGORY FINAL-ROUND PRIZE POOL Bright Data $60,000 in software credits + $6,000 in cash Algolia $40,000 in software credits. Neo4j $6,000 in software credits. Storyblok $3,000 in cash. HackerNoon $3,000 in cash. articles.title: Reddit Will Force Everyone to Log In
articles.content: Reddit plans to require users to log in to browse the platform, ending its longstanding practice of allowing anonymous visitors to access posts and discussions. According to CEO Steve Huffman, a key reason behind the decision is to curb unauthorized scraping and automated traffic. "This is a big change for Reddit, where we've allowed logged-out access to basically all of Reddit for the last two decades," Huffman says. "And I don't know about you, but as someone whose life has been defined by the open internet, it's a big change for me. But I've come to the conclusion that this is the right decision for our platform and the right decision for our business." The Verge reports: There's no definitive timeline on when this change will roll out to all users, or how the site will work if you're logged out. (If I send my friend a link to a thread and they aren't logged in, what will they see?) To start, Reddit will test the logged-in requirement in "select markets outside the US" in the "coming months," according to CEO Steve Huffman. "We'll look at the impact on the user experience, on our business, and on the whole Reddit ecosystem, figure out where the right boundaries are, and go from there." Reddit has also rebuilt and is rereleasing the Reddit app's incognito mode. Huffman claims the login requirement is better for Reddit's user experience and its ads business and is "more protective of Reddit data." The "vast majority" of unauthorized Reddit access happens "through our logged-out experiences," though the company will still strike licensing deals of its data with companies, like the deals it made with OpenAI and Google in 2024. Huffman notes that Reddit does not need to know a logged-in user's identity -- "Honestly, we don't want to know" -- just that the user is logged in at all. And he says that more logged-in users lets the company deliver "more relevant ads." Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.content: It's Halloween, so it's a great time to make sure you're not getting tricked out of your hard-earned cash and cancel those subscriptions you've forgotten about. Here's how to do it. Why and how you should audit your subscriptions Digital hygiene, the practice of keeping a clean, safe digital footprint, is critical for anyone who uses the internet — which is pretty much everyone. Many things fall under the digital hygiene umbrella, from responsible email management to removing your data from data brokerage companies' websites. There are many digital hygiene tasks you should do at least twice a year. For instance, you're probably going to want to check to make sure none of your passwords have wound up in a data breach. articles.title: Google just gave students access to hundreds of textbooks in Gemini Notebook — here's how it can help you study smarter
articles.content: What was once known as Google’s NotebookLM has now become Gemini Notebook , an easily accessible and private resource for deep research sessions. Being able to produce your notebooks by uploading files, including links to numerous sites, attaching purchases from your Books on Google Play account and more has highlighted just how useful Gemini Notebook truly is. Its studio features have proven to be equally valuable, as Gemini Notebook users can turn their research guides into a video overview, an audio overview, a slide deck, flashcards and so much more. A May 2026 Gemini Notebook update introduced Expert Intelligence, which lets users use select ebooks from Google Play Books, third-party subscriptions and more. Now, the latest update has arrived in Gemini Notebook and is giving students and other users of the platform access to hundreds of textbooks. Here’s how that new feature can improve how you study even more. Even more reliable sources are now housed within Gemini Notebook (Image credit: Shutterstock) Gemini Notebook now has a vast library of textbooks that have been provided by companies based in the US and India. Those companies include Open Textbook Library, S Chand Publishing and OpenStax. And thankfully, that newly added feature comes free of charge. Utilizing this feature is as easy as opening a new or existing Gemini Notebook, clicking on “Add Sources” and clicking on “Textbooks.” The textbooks on offer are split across the following categories: Business Computer science Economics Engineering Health & Medicine History & Philosophy Languages & Writing Law & Politics Life Sciences Mathematics Physical Sciences Psychology Sociology & Culture Student Success Other After perusing some of the newly added textbooks myself, I spotted a bunch of sources that stand out as quality guides for users who want to dip their toes into certain topics. With the help of Gemini itself, I discovered a few of the top OpenStax textbooks you can access right now: Biology 2e / AP® Biology: Covers cell division, metabolic pathways, molecular genetics, and ecology. Ideal for asking for breakdown explanations of complex diagrams or generating practice questions. Chemistry 2e / AP® Chemistry: Includes stoichiometry, thermochemistry, equilibrium, and periodic trends. Very useful for step-by-step problem-solving breakdowns. Psychology 2e: Spans cognitive psychology, neurological structures, behavioral science, and developmental stages. Works well with interactive Q&A for comparative theoretical frameworks. Introduction to Business & Principles of Management: Focuses on organizational structure, financial basics, leadership frameworks, and business ethics. Great for generating executive summaries and briefing docs. Principles of Economics (Macro & Micro): Details supply-demand elasticity, market structures, fiscal policy, and monetary systems. Bottom line All in all, Gemini Notebook’s new lineup of textbooks that can be used as reliable sources is another boon to an already great AI tool. I’ve dabbled in a bunch of the pre-made notebooks that offer extensive deep dives into topics such as creating better habits for oneself to succeed, the best movies of the 21st century, the ultimate guide to home buying and William Shakespeare’s complete works. If I ever get the urge to begin my analysis of Psychology, I’m going to take a trip over to Google Notebook to build a guide for myself that includes pertinent info from one of its many reliable textbooks. articles.title: How to turn a Siri Remote into a handy Mac controller
articles.content: A Siri Remote can make controlling a Mac from across the room much easier, and with one utility you can use it as a small trackpad, although you'll need more than macOS's built-in support to get the full experience. Siri Remote with Mac If your Mac mini is connected to a TV, or you use your MacBook for presentations, reaching for a keyboard to control playback isn't always convenient. An Apple TV Siri Remote lets you manage basic controls from across the room without returning to your Mac. A Siri Remote connects to a Mac over Bluetooth, and macOS already supports some of its buttons. However, Apple designed the remote for Apple TV, so its clickpad doesn't automatically control the mouse or navigate Mac apps. Basic controls work without additional software, while third-party apps add more functionality. Whether it's worth setting up depends on how much control you need and whether you're willing to switch the remote between your Mac and Apple TV. articles.title: Voyager 1 gives controllers the silent treatment
articles.content: Voyager 1 gave controllers the silent treatment for a few days this month before resuming communication weeks before the spacecraft reaches the one-light-day milestone. The incident happened on October 18: NASA's Deep Space Network (DSN) couldn't detect a signal from the probe. On October 19, on the next scheduled communication attempt, there was still nothing. Was this it? Had the decades-long galactic venture finally ended? Things are operating on a knife's edge for the two veteran spacecraft, which will reach their half-century next year. Voyager 2 suffered an antenna pointing issue in 2023, and a low power condition caused Voyager 1 to unexpectedly turn off one of its two radio transmitters. The good news is that on October 20, the signal reappeared, leaving engineers wondering why Voyager 1 temporarily went silent. Thus far, it seems a group of thrusters went offline and their backups were turned on. This could indicate onboard computers detected a problem and put the spacecraft into a safe mode. Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, said: "This is the first time we've seen the spacecraft do something like this, but we are also at a point in the mission where we have to expect the unexpected. "We're relieved to be back in contact with Voyager 1 and are eager to understand what happened." The Register spoke to Badaruddin in 2024 , where he described the challenges of working with the veteran spacecraft, but he reckoned the work was the "best job at JPL." The twin Voyager spacecraft have recently been through a procedure dubbed the "Big Bang," where controllers turned off onboard devices and switched to lower power alternatives. The result will extend the lifetime of the spacecraft by a few more years and postpone further instrument deactivation. It was completed first on Voyager 2, and then Voyager 1, six weeks later in September. However, the brief lapse in communication highlights that despite the ingenuity of the team that keep the spacecraft running, the project must eventually come to an end. In 2026, Suzanne Dodd, Project Manager for the Voyager project, told The Register what the end would look like . She said, "We're just going to one day not hear the signal from the DSN, and we're going to rush around and make sure that it's not something on the ground." Months of listening will follow, before engineers throw in the towel and declare the mission over. And then? Maybe a farewell message sent to the last known location. Thankfully, in this case, the signal returned, so no need for a goodbye transmission just yet. In a few weeks, Voyager 1 will be so far away that it will take a full 24 hours for commands to reach it and another 24 hours for a response to reach Earth. Communications blip notwithstanding, there is every chance both Voyager spacecraft will still be operational as they pass their half-century milestone next year and, technology and funding permitting, continue sending data to Earth for a good few years yet. ®

articles.title: Binance Suffers Biggest Crypto Hack In History With $6.3 Billion Affected [UPDATE]
articles.content: UPDATE 10/30/26: Binance has temporarily suspended customer withdrawals after suffering what investigators say is the biggest crypto hack in history. According to Binance CEO Yi He, the company estimates roughly $6.3 billion in funds were impacted, with roughly $3 billion in assets frozen on-chain so far. Rest assured, "your money is safe, and we're covering every loss," said co-CEO Richard Teng in a LinkedIn post. "This was a complex attack," said Teng. "The attacker also used a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and tracers, making it more difficult for us to trace." From a report: Teng said the incident was not carried out by one person. While the initial investigation indicated the involvement of a compromised laptop, further digging revealed additional points of breach. [...] Blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Elliptic have linked the theft to North Korean hackers, with TRM attributing it "with high confidence" to a group known as TraderTraitor, the same group responsible for last year's Bybit hack. Elliptic estimated Friday that about 44% of the stolen assets have been frozen, with stablecoins accounting for nearly all of those funds. The firm estimated that attackers still controlled over $3 billion in crypto that token issuers cannot directly freeze. The hackers appear to have compromised Binance's wallet-signing infrastructure, allowing them to authorize transactions that drained billions of dollars in cryptocurrency across multiple blockchains, according to the firms. Binance, in its preliminary stage, has conducted an investigation into the hack, which suggests the incident may have begun with a compromised engineer's laptop. The exchange added that it has found no evidence that wallet passwords were leaked. Below is the original story from yesterday, Oct. 29th. Binance is investigating a potential hack after more than $2 billion in crypto was drained from one of its wallets into a new external account, with Blockaid estimating nearly $3.3 billion was moved. "Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating," said Binance on X. "User funds are safe," said Binance founder CZ. "It does look like a hack on Binance. Appreciate the quick freeze from Tether (~$971m) and Circle (~$823m). I don't manage Binance anymore, but as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered." At around the same time, crypto-based prediction market Polymarket reported its own security incident that wiped out around $2.7 million in user funds. Read more of this story at Slashdot.
